newsitem.title: USA: Wyser-Pratte says Rexene move not enough.
newsitem.headline: Wyser-Pratte says Rexene move not enough.

text.p: Dissident Rexene Corp shareholder Wyser-Pratte said an announcement from Rexene that it would hold a Dutch auction for 11.5 percent of its shares instead of an open market offer was a victory for shareholders, but did not end the need to remove the company's board.

"The initial share repurchase programme had been targetted at our supporters, now those investors who accept the tender will be able to vote at Rexene's special meeting on April 30," said Eric Longmeire, managing director of Wyser-Pratte.

Wyser-Pratte said it had complained to the U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC) about Rexene's initial programme and it believed that the SEC had been instrumental in forcing Rexene's change.
Wyser-Pratte and its allies hold around 13 percent of Rexene.
Citing a letter from former Rexene board member Arthur Goeschel to the SEC, Longmeire told Reuters that "Goeschel blew the whistle on the Rexene board", a charge that Rexene strongly denied.
"The decision to make a tender was made by board based on relatively low response to the open offer, Wyser-Pratte's allegations about the SEC are false," said a spokesman for Rexene.
Rexene said in a statement that the Dutch Auction at $14 to $16 a share would replace the first part of a planned $85 million stock repurchase program announced on March 19.
Just 11,500 shares were purchase between March 24 and March 27 under the old offer.
Rexene said that it was committed to shareholder value and would actively consider any fully-financed all-cash offers for the company.
Asked to comment on whether privately-held Huntsman Chemical had made a firm offer, Rexene said that there were no firm bids on the table.
"Mister Huntsman is very good at issuing press releases, but if he were truly interested in making an offer he should do so," said the Rexene spokesman.
Wyser-Pratte said that it believed that other companies would be interested in Rexene.

"After it (the auction) is over, there will be an even more compelling need to replace the board and sell the company since Rexene will be weighed down with another $35 million of debt it can ill afford to service, which is an issue that Goeschel resigned over," said Wyser-Pratte's Longmeire.
